mainEntity.name: Do regional climate conditions in Northern and Central Arizona affect how skim coating cures?

acceptedAnswer.text: In northern and central Arizona communities like Flagstaff, Prescott, and Sedona, wide daily temperature swings and seasonal shifts between dry winters and humid summer monsoons affect compound cure rates. Joint compound must dry evenly to avoid edge shrinkage, cracking, or surface chalking. During winter months at higher elevations, interior heating must remain stable overnight so coats cure properly. During dry spells in lower elevation areas like Camp Verde or Cottonwood, thin coats can dry too quickly on unprimed surfaces, making it essential to prime exposed drywall cores beforehand.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, elevation, winter cold, and monsoon humidity affect compound cure rates, requiring controlled indoor temperatures and proper wall priming to prevent cracking or premature drying.
